title: Know what's behind your smart lockers—not just what's inside them
summary: The best smart locker solution should make things easier on both sides of the locker door, helping staff process deliveries quickly while giving recipients a convenient pickup experience.
body_markdown:
### **2. Make sure the software supports your entire package operation**


Behind every smart locker system is software that controls how packages are received, stored, tracked and picked up.


Look for a vendor that offers more than basic locker management. Ideally, the software should support your entire inbound package process, from the moment a package arrives until it reaches the recipient.


Integrated package tracking and smart lockers on the same platform can give your team one place to manage deliveries, whether they're placed in a locker, picked-up at a service counter or delivered directly to a department.


Rather than switching between systems or tracking packages manually, staff can work from one platform with better visibility and control across the entire operation.


### **3. Access to reporting and analytics for smarter decision making**


Smart lockers can do more than store packages. They can also provide valuable insights into your operation.


Look for a vendor that offers robust reporting and analytics, ideally within the same platform used to manage your packages and lockers.


With the right data, you can answer questions like:


- Which locker locations fill up the fastest?
- When are package volumes highest?
- How long do packages typically remain in lockers?
- Do we have enough capacity to handle peak periods?


For example, a university mail center might discover that packages sit in certain lockers longer than others or can easily identify repeat offenders who leave them there. They could show the peak delivery and pick-up times. These insights could help the team schedule staff accordingly, adjust pickup reminders or make better use of available space.


When package tracking and locker analytics work together, you get a more complete picture of your operation and can help you make better decisions about staffing, capacity and future investments.


### **4. Service that doesn't stop at installation.**


Even the best technology needs support from time to time.


When a locker isn't working properly, it can create headaches for staff and recipients alike. That's why it's important to understand what happens after installation.


Does the vendor offer technical support? Can they troubleshoot issues remotely? If a repair is needed, how quickly can someone get there?


An established vendor with a nationwide service organization and local technicians can provide added peace of mind. Having trained representatives nearby can help resolve issues faster, reduce downtime and keep packages moving.


Also consider installation, training, software updates and ongoing maintenance. You want a partner that will be there as your needs change, not just one that delivers the lockers and moves on.


### **5. Choose a vendor with proven industry experience**


There's a difference between a company that offers locker hardware and one that truly understands package management.


An established vendor with a long history in shipping and mailing understands the challenges of handling high package volumes, tracking deliveries and keeping busy mailrooms running smoothly.


That experience matters because every organization handles packages differently. A college mail center managing thousands of student deliveries has different needs than a corporate office or apartment building.


Consider the vendor's track record. Have they worked with organizations like yours? Do they have the resources, technology and service network to support your investment over time?


Remember, you're not just simply buying lockers. You're choosing a partner you can count on for years to come. **


### **Choose a partner, not just a product**


Smart lockers are an investment in more efficient inbound package management. But getting the most from that investment takes more than choosing the right number of compartments.


The vendor's industry experience, software, workflows, analytics and service capabilities all matter.


When comparing solutions, ask vendors to demonstrate how packages are received, loaded, tracked and picked up. Explore the reporting tools and understand what support you can expect down the road.


The right vendor won't just help you manage packages today. They'll help you build a smarter, more efficient operation for years to come.
